_comment: Capability comparison shown on the Features & roadmap page. Generated once, offline, from the competitor audit (private repo concurrentie-analyse). The audit is not public, so this file is committed rather than built in CI. Regenerate by hand when a new round lands. `comparedOn` is the date the FIRST FOUR columns were read and it moves only when all four are read again. A column added later carries its own `readOn` and its own `columnAddedOn`, because moving `comparedOn` to cover it would make the reading-date sentence false for the four it already covers. A column added after the LIST grew is `unknown` on the rows it was never read against, the same rule the competitor columns follow. `rowsAddedOn` is the date rows were LAST added to the LIST, which is a different event: a later round can ask a new question without re-reading the older products. More than one round has now done so, so a row carries its OWN `addedOn` and `rowsAddedOn` is the most recent of them. A row added that way carries `addedOn` and rates EVERY competitor `unknown`, because a guess in someone else's column is worse than an empty cell. Our OWN column is corrected between rounds, because a rating that says we lack something we shipped is the one error on this page a reader cannot check for themselves. Every correction and every added row is listed in `_rerated` with its date and its reason, and `reratedOn` carries the latest. The competitor columns are NOT corrected that way: we would be re-reading someone else's product without saying so, and the honest fix for those is a new round with a new comparedOn.

_rerated.reason: Plan follow-up is a header action on the case page, swept by a background job. A repeating series still is not, so this is partial and not yes.
A case carries tags, edited in the Tags sidebar tab and filtered on the Cases list.
Copy case is a header action on the case page, backed by CaseCopyService.
A document carries keywords, shown as chips on its row and offered as a filter over the case file.
A protected person is marked as protected, their number is masked, and revealing it writes an audit row.
Case types group into folders by category. Attributes and templates do not, so this is partial and not yes.
Round 3 row. Two reports of the same nuisance on two channels is routine front-office work. We relate cases, we never collapse them, and a late reply to the closed one reaches nobody.
Round 3 row. Nothing on our intake path looks for a case that already exists.
Round 3 row, narrowed. The proposal also asked whether the pause reason is stored, which row 2.11 already asks. What is left is the chasing, and nothing in the app re-asks.

Round 3 row. CaseRelationService types a link as vervolg, subject or bijdrage and writes it on both cases, but the mirror carries the same name, so no link means blocks on one side and blocked by on the other.
Round 3 row, refiled from access-and-privacy to case-core: a lock is concurrency, not access control. Two handlers can overwrite each other on a case and neither is told.
Round 3 row. Our bulk actions each do one thing, and none of them decides where the handler lands afterwards.
Round 3 row. One flag per entry is what makes a single timeline safe to show an applicant. Row 6.4 is already no for the timeline, so the flag was never in question.
Round 3 row, refiled from integrations to communication. We score no and we are content with it: a municipality owes an applicant an outcome, not a rating request.
Round 3 row. Article 1 of the Algemene termijnenwet extends a term that ends on a Saturday, Sunday or recognised holiday. We add the days and stop.

Round 3 row. Round 3 read five private calendars and rated us no. WorkingDayCalculator has since landed and all five callers use it, so the single source of truth exists. Nobody can edit a holiday without a release, so this is partial and not yes.
Round 3 row, and one we lead on. DeadlinePauseService moves the end date out and pulls back the unused part when the applicant answers early, which is what Awb 4:15 asks for.

Round 3 row. DeadlineEscalationService widens from handler to teamleader to manager at 14, 7, 2 and 0 days. The ladder is a constant in code and not yet administered, which is a refinement rather than a gap.
Round 3 row. TermijnService stores both end dates as a date. A Dutch term expires at the close of a day, so storing a timestamp would be wrong here.
Round 3 row. Our threshold alerts sit on complaint analytics, not on a saved search.

Round 3 row. Round 3 rated us no and missed the Hours booked tile, which now books hours and runs a timer against the case. The hours live in humaniq and there is no rate or cost model, so this is partial and not yes.
Round 3 row. We hide actions and widgets on a field value, and field permissions exist per role, but no rule combines the two and none of it makes a field mandatory.
Round 3 row. Answers reused across cases are most of what a contact centre does, and we have no place to keep them.
Round 3 row. Row 13.12 covers mandates and deputies as a delegation of rights. This asks whether a case assigned to someone on leave shows up on anybody's list, and it does not.
Round 3 row. A favourite is navigation and row 2.19 already asks about it. A watch is a subscription, and a jurist following a sensitive case has no way to ask for one.

DeadlinePauseService::resumeAfterPauze credits the unused pause back when the aanvulling arrives, which is the clock half. No object represents the request, so nobody can list the cases waiting on an applicant.

ZgwRulesBase::checkFieldUniqueness refuses a colliding write on the ZGW path. It refuses rather than returning the candidates, there is no override the writer records, and it does not run outside ZGW.

case.priority is a fixed four-value enum and the queue weights are a private constant in WorkQueueService. The LHS matrix is a genuine two-axis administered scheme, and it derives an intervention rather than a priority.

CaseCopyService opens a second, separately numbered case and writes a typed vervolg relation back to the source, and DeelzaakService splits off a sub-case. Documents are linked whole rather than apportioned, and parties are not divided at all.
Row 2.8 tags are free labels anyone can remove silently. Nothing demands a written reason on raising or clearing, and nothing attributes either act.
CaseTransferService moves a case between organisations and writes an audit entry. There is no dated ownership history you can read back as a chain, so who held the case in March is not a query.
CaseTransferService only pushes a case away. Nothing lets a colleague pull one, and there is no accept or refuse with a reason on the holder's side.
ConsultationService::getBlockingConsultations blocks on an open advice request. Nothing generalises that to other dependencies, and the closing statuses are still offered rather than withheld.

lhsRecommendation carries a severity read by LhsLookupService, but it is scoped to VTH. It is not on the case schema, it is not separately permissioned, and it drives neither priority nor filtering, so all three qualifiers of the row fail.
BulkStatusTransitionService pairs a preview with an execute and has no inverse and no stored batch record. A mistake on a hundred cases is a hundred manual corrections.

The workflow editor and the board are keyboard operable and spec'd as such, which is accessibility rather than this capability. There is no command palette and no global shortcut layer anywhere in src/.
StateMachineService moves a case when somebody chooses a transition. Nothing computes the status from which forms and documents are present.
Row 2.30 is a marker a person raises on the whole case. This is one the system raises against a specific tab and drops when the work behind that tab is done.
A case holds one situation. Nothing models several dated incidents inside it, each with its own owner and its own transfer, which is how repeat reports on one address are handled elsewhere.

statusType.role is an administered enum including pending-info and stranded, rendered as Waiting for information and read by StatusTypeLookup and the shipped flow. It conflates waiting on the applicant with waiting on a third party, and no team count is built on it.
ComplaintService has a withdrawn status, set internally by a handler. No case type lets the applicant close their own case from the portal.
Row 2.26 declares typed links. Nothing walks them to answer who else is affected, and nothing lets you prune a branch of that walk.
CaseNumberService issues a number without a locked counter row. The demo data already shows identifier reading a dash on five of seven cases, so the weakness is visible rather than theoretical.

No If-Match, ETag or expected version exists on any write, so the last save wins silently. conflictRecord is declared in the offline sync fragment and has no reader. Row 2.27 answers the same problem with a lock, which is the heavier of the two designs.
CaseTransferService carries the whole hand-off: offer, acceptance, rejection and the audit entry for each. Added so the instrument can record a strength, not only a gap.
DispositionService gates a complaint disposition on an approval. It resolves no manager from the organisation tree and no other case type can use it.
Routing/Strategy has RoundRobin and LeastLoaded. There is no per-person weight, no way to target a named position inside a team, and no condition that takes work back.

WorkflowBoard.vue groups by status into columns on one axis, so there are no swimlanes. Its drop handler writes case.status straight to OpenRegister and never reaches TransitionAuthorizer, so a drag is not restricted by role at all.

milestoneDefinition declares dependsOn and nothing reads it: offsets are a cumulative sum from the case start ordered by a number. Neither milestoneDefinition nor deadlineInstance carries an assignee, so nothing resolves one from a role on the case.
Row 8.4 reminders fire at a date. A planned next action is a typed record with an owner that, on completion, schedules the one that follows it.
Tasks carry due dates and assignees, not dependencies. Nothing derives a blocked state and nothing releases it without a person noticing.
ConsultationService blocks a case on an advice request and releases it. Nothing generalises the pattern to any other obligation, so each new one is a new service.
SubstitutionService and MandaatEscalatieService exist. Nothing declares what happens when an approver says nothing, and nothing asks a substitute before the timeout runs out.
ConsultationService carries the question, the attachments, the deadline, the blocking behaviour, the extension request and its approval. Added so the instrument can record a strength.

The informatieobject already carries a direction, incoming, outgoing or internal, and a registration date. document.identifier has no generator, so there is no gapless year and unit scoped number, and no outbound entry discharging an inbound one.

Qualified signing ships per beschikking, through the signing adapter and the mandaat check. Nothing gathers documents from several cases into one pass, and a wethouder signing forty decisions opens forty cases.
Rows 4.4 and 11.11 ask whether a letter can be generated. Nothing asks whether it can be understood, and for a decision carrying a bezwaartermijn that is a legal interest.
Row 2.24 asks about duplicate cases. Nothing finds two records of the same person, and nothing merges them field by field with a refusal when the merger cannot see every domain involved.
Without this a deduplication screen offers the same false pair every week until people stop reading it. It is what makes row 5.14 usable rather than a second capability on top of it.
Row 5.1 gives a party a role on a case. Nothing relates two parties to each other, so guardian and ward, or employer and employee, cannot be stated.
The party model carries no language and the email templates carry no locale. document.language exists and is an attribute of the file, not a preference of the person we are writing to.

sociaalDomeinAuditLog.authorisationGround is declared in the register and no code reads it. Row 5.4 asks for the opposite thing, a full 360 view, which purpose limitation does not allow between Wmo, Jeugdwet and Participatiewet.
Rows 5.3 and 5.11 ask whether we can look a person up in BRP or KvK. 25-brp-kvk.json carries no readOnlyFromSource, no policy for a record that disappears, and no lock against a manual delete.
statusType carries one name, so whatever a caseworker calls a status is what a citizen reads in the portal. Two systems in the corpus invented the split independently.
InboundEmailJob matches on mailMessageId only. In-Reply-To and References appear nowhere, and quoted text and signatures are not stripped, so a reply chain lands as repeated text.
CaseEmailService sends to the recipients the case implies. There is no way to add a person to one message only, or to leave one out and record that you did.

The beschikking dispatch record carries receipt and read confirmation dates, and BerichtenboxService writes readAt. The job that would poll it is deliberately not registered and has never run on any instance, and nothing rolls up to a sortable field on the case.
ContactMomentService files a contact onto one case. One phone call about three cases becomes three records that then drift apart.
NotificatieService sends on events the code decides. An administrator cannot say which field change notifies whom, and recipients are not derived from the case.

DeliveryConcludedListener does project status, attempts and error onto the case's publication record, and Berichtenbox polls a read flag per message, so the proposal's claim that bounces appear only in a comment is wrong. No channel reports per recipient and nothing reaches a case list column, so the row is still no.
Row 13.18 watchers is itself no, so nobody subscribes to anything yet. Nothing marks a kind as never reaching the external party, and nothing lets an administrator say this one always goes by post.

30-beschikking.json declares the beschikking immutable once signed, StateMachineService pins four immutable statuses, BeschikkingService::updateFields throws on a content field at or after signed, and the controller answers 409. decisionType already carries amendment. What is missing is the pointer at the record it replaces and the derived successor number.

The committees register models bezwaaradviescommissie and bacAdviceRequest, and BezwaarDecisionDelegationService and AdviceDelegationService carry the round trip. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
ComplaintService computes an acknowledgement deadline from a private constant, for complaints and nothing else. Nothing measures whether it was met and nothing stores how late we were.
StalledCaseDetector projects the earliest unreached milestone from the case start and reports a case past a grace period. No status carries a configured maximum time of its own.

WorkingDayCalculator is day-level by design and there is one global calendar. Row 8.12 asks for that one calendar to be administered; this asks for hours inside the day and for more than one set of them.
Row 2.26 declares typed links and none of them carries a scheduling consequence. When a predecessor slips two weeks, every dependent date is corrected by hand or not at all.
Row 8.4 reminders attach to a case with a responsible user. They cannot bind to an arbitrary date field, cannot repeat, and cannot stop themselves when the thing they chase is done.
Row 8.1 puts the term on the case type, so one shared case type cannot carry different terms for different participating municipalities. This is the gemeenschappelijke-regeling shape.
DeadlinePauseService and DeadlineEscalationService do this imperatively, with thresholds in days rather than as a share of the term. Nothing declares which statuses the clock runs in.

statusRecord stores every transition as a queryable object with fromStatus, and process mining reads it. There is still no case list filter of the form was ever in status X, and giving this partial credit would double count row 10.4, which already scores that surface.
Nothing lets an administrator teach the search that omgevingsvergunning and bouwvergunning are the same thing to a citizen typing in the portal.

The beschikking state machine log carries actorType, employee or systeem, and trigger, manual or automatic, written by BeschikkingService and read by AuditPacketBuilder. It is a two-value axis on one subsystem, with no import, migration or cascade cause, and the general trail is OpenRegister's.
Row 10.11 asks whether time can be booked against a case and is partial. Nothing holds an estimate, so nothing can say how much of it is left.

DwellTimeAnalyzer computes dwell per case and status visit and aggregates median, p90 and mean, charted on the process mining page. The number is not held on the case, so a handler cannot sort or filter a work list by it.
Row 11.18 detects configuration problems and is yes. Nothing defines a population of records, runs rules over it and scores the result against a tolerance.

Routing/Strategy holds Hierarchical, LeastLoaded, OrSet, RoundRobin and SingleRole, and PdokService resolves an address without boundaries. districtTeam is declared with no PHP reader, and the wijk and buurt selection is a written spec scenario nothing implements.
Row 11.2 exports and imports case types. Nothing tracks that a municipality changed a published one, so an update either overwrites the local change or is never applied.
Row 11.25 hides and requires fields by role and case state. Nothing makes a field required because another field holds a particular value, and nothing enforces that on a write that skips the form.

Resolved rather than assumed: StatusTransitionService re-evaluates the identical guard set on the POST transition path and throws GuardFailedException, so the rules do run server-side. It stays partial because the set is transition-scoped rather than per field on every write, and the board's drop handler bypasses it entirely.
An import runs and reports at the end. Nothing survives it, so nobody can go back to a load from last month and see which rows failed and why.
Row 11.20 rules stand alone. Without composition, the same condition is written out in twenty rules and corrected in nineteen of them.
statusType.description exists and nothing renders it. There is no text on a transition at all, so the moment a handler is choosing is the moment with no guidance.
Nothing lets an administrator nominate a field as effectively unique and get a warning on save. A second case on the same KvK number is found later or never.
Rows 11.6 to 11.9 are all no, so there is no screen configuration to store yet. This is the mechanism to build them in, because the alternative drops a customer's change silently at the next release.
Row 11.20 rules read current values, so moved into this status and is in this status are the same condition. The first fires once, the second fires every time anything is saved.
Row 11.3 custom fields per case type is yes, and only an administrator can add one. A team that needs one field waits for a change request.
Row 11.23 groups case types into folders for administrators. This is the citizen-facing side of the same object, and it is what makes a term resolvable per service rather than per case type.
Row 11.10 code lists are flat and fixed. A field cannot offer only the contacts of the organisation already chosen on this case.

workflowTemplate.lifecycleStatus carries deprecated, described as cannot back new cases while existing cases keep using it, and WorkflowDefinitionService enforces it and refuses a deprecation that would strand open cases. There is no equivalent for arbitrary code list values, and caseType.validUntil is shown but not enforced as a picker filter.
Rows 11.20 and 3.11 ask whether rules exist. Nothing records that one ran, so why did this case not get its letter has no answer short of reading the code.
A rule cannot say created more than three working hours ago, so time-based escalation is written as jobs rather than as configuration a manager can change.
Rows 11.6 to 11.9 are all no. One screen for handlers, a narrower one for the front office and a third for the portal is the ordinary requirement, and there is no shape for it.
Row 11.10 is flat and each entry is a label. Nothing hangs a term, a route or a required document off the value the handler picks.
FieldValidator and StepConfigValidator validate what the code says. An administrator cannot add a check, and cannot write the sentence the handler reads when it fails.

WorkflowStepAuthorizationResolver reads each transition's allowed roles and WorkflowDefinitionService::publish writes the resolved group ids into the transition, which OpenRegister enforces server-side. Added so the instrument can record a strength.

Mandaat is modelled and MandaatVerifier reads it, and ConflictOfInterestService asks whether a handler is related to the applicant. No transition carries a negative flag, so nothing stops the person who wrote a decision from approving it.

Row 13.4 grants access, by somebody else, with no reason and no per-case-type switch. sociaalDomeinAuditLog.authorisationGround is declared in the register and has zero readers, so there is no time box, no reason and no access level per case type.

toestemming is declared in the sociaal domein register and the only toestemming hits in lib/ are Dutch error strings. CaseTransferService::initiateTransfer has no consent branch and createPartnerShare writes a share with no scope, so nothing is ever blocked.
Rows 8.7 and 13.10 delete on a retention schedule. An erasure request names a person and has to reach identifiers inside message bodies and mail headers, and report honestly what it could not remove.
Row 5.1 puts parties on a case with roles. Rights are granted to people and groups, not to the slot, so replacing the occupant means editing every grant.
Rows 8.7 and 13.10 destroy on a date. A vernietigingslijst is reviewed item by item by a named reviewer and a co-reviewer, and each response is recorded before anything is destroyed.
anonymisationAtParts has zero readers, and ArchivalNominationDeriver's whole action vocabulary is bewaren, blijvend_bewaren and vernietigen. There is no anonymise branch to configure.

The Wet bescherming klokkenluiders obliges a municipality to run exactly this surface. Nothing accepts a report against a receipt code, and nothing gates the reveal on a motivated request a custodian answers.
A gemachtigde, a guardian or a parent company should see the record they are entitled to see because of the relationship. Access is granted per case and per user instead.

AuditPacketBuilder assembles the beschikking, its immutable transition log and a validation report into a ZIP and stamps it with a sha256 digest, routed at /api/beschikkingen/{id}/audit-pakket. It is a per-beschikking export, not a chained log over the whole trail, and no previousHash exists anywhere.
Row 2.26 declares typed links. A link is all or nothing, so relating a Wmo case to a Jeugdwet case exposes everything or nothing rather than the two fields that were meant.
Rows 13.2 and 13.16 ask whether the rules exist and can be administered. Neither asks whether a caseworker can find out why they cannot see something, so every denial becomes a support ticket.
Row 13.13 grants portal rights per case. A holding company with eleven subsidiaries is then eleven separate grants, maintained by hand as the group changes.
Row 13.9 logs a read. lib/Notification holds only the notifier and no download listener is registered, so nothing acts on one while it is happening.

The case schema says of the team that it is assignment, not permission. Reassignment is gated by a coordinator check that resolves to isAdmin, so handing work over is an admin right rather than an axis of its own beside read and write.
Rows 13.3 and 13.6 are both partial. Nothing says where a permission came from, and nothing marks one as not inheritable, so an access review cannot be finished.
CaseSharingService::createTokenShare issues the link and revokeTokenShare withdraws it, both with an expiry. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
LegalHoldApplier, BezwaarLegalHoldListener and AwbProceedingScanner place and lift the hold as a bezwaar or beroep opens and closes. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
CaseReassignmentService and SelectionReassignmentService move a whole caseload at once, by handler or by selection. Added so the instrument can record a strength.

The register declares gezinsplan.goals and deploymentTrajectories as plain string arrays, with no provider, no target date and no completion mark, and nothing reads them. The schema cannot express the row, so this is no and not partial.

The Subsidie services carry the whole arc: award, interim reporting, final determination, evidence, co-financing and recovery, with the Dwangsom services beside them. Added so the instrument can record a strength.

dossiq registers the field-inspection leaf with its own offline config, and the leaf owns the queue and the replay. Its own Dexie store, sync queue engine, replay service and controller were deleted, so conflictRecord has no reader and an inspector still cannot work without a signal.
Twenty Tenant services carry it, including TenantSchemaProvisioner, TenantQuotaService and TenantAuditTrailService. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
